source_record.inference: The explicit contribution is material at its stated guard even when final action is confirmed rather than changed. Corresponding mechanisms may overlap; duplicate names, reused tests and common pipelines do not create additional benefit or independence.
attempted_contrary_interfaces: Identical test behavior treated as unique artifact identity.
A green pipeline treated as exposure authority.
An approved model treated as actual deployed state.
The same test counted as independent evidence twice.
All evidence discarded after harmless change.
All evidence carried after a changed critical premise.
A trace link treated as proof of the linked claim.

positive_controls.argument: Maintained build rationale, dependency meaning and repair responsibility let another engineer reproduce and interpret the integrated state.
Unique revisions, reproducible build inputs and baseline status identify which shared state participants integrated and tested.
Delegated change classes and affected-evidence analysis identify what may merge routinely and what requires additional review or bounded staging.
Contract versions, shared ownership and compatibility policy determine the integration boundary and legitimate handling of incompatible evolution.
Risk-relevant conditions and feasible verification methods define the health checks needed for the next integration decision.
Accurate requirement, interface and evidence links identify the integration checks affected by a change and support reuse of unaffected results.
The argument exposes which integration assumptions matter and which failure must block the claimed assurance conclusion.
The anomaly history preserves the affected configurations, temporary reversal and residual work so integration recovery is not misreported as full problem closure.
Scoped authority, version relationships and model semantics identify the correct representations and generated products for integration.
Controlled execution, trustworthy evidence provenance and prompt consuming decisions support the health and usefulness of repeated mainline verification.
